messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: synch RStan/Stan + major.minor.patch numbering
parts:
I'm very psyched to hear that we'll be in synch to start,
so the comments I added below are forward looking.

On 8/27/12 4:52 PM, Ben Goodrich wrote:
> On Monday, August 27, 2012 3:54:54 PM UTC-4, Bob Carpenter wrote:
>
> Everyone: should we coordinate the releases?
>
>
> I would say that every Stan release should imply a new rstan release, although it may occasionally be necessary to
> release a new rstan without releasing a new Stan (due to CRAN policy changes, changes in packages rstan depends on, bugs
> in R code, etc.)

I would like to stick to a

major.minor.patch

release numbering scheme, with any change in
documented functionality implying at least a
minor version update.

I only care that Stan/RStan numberings synch
so that any RStan major.minor version will run
any major/minor-matching Stan version.

So I wouldn't have minded releasing Stan 1.0.0
when we're only up to RStan 1.0.beta.

The problem I see with Stan getting ahead of RStan
on minor version number is people reading the wrong
doc. The install of RStan is encapsulated, so that
shouldn't cause a problem.

- Bob

messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: Re: [stan-dev] Stan 1.0.0 release this week?
parts:
On 8/27/12 5:50 PM, Marcus Brubaker wrote:
> Ok, I've pushed the bug fix and the positive_ordered type. It
> includes unit tests, source level docs and a note in the language
> section of the docs.
That's great.

> When/If we add bound constraints to the basic ordered type
> positive_ordered can become a synonym or removed depending on how
> widely it gets used.

I'm for making it a synonym later.

I'd rather not break backward compatibility for
models unless we absolutely have to.

And then, I'd rather break backward compatibiltiy in
two stages, first by deprecating the old behavior in
the current major version, then updating to a major
version that removed deprecated functions. That gives
users a clear upgrade path with warnings in their code
to help guide their fixes.

- Bob

I was just thinking about something about CRAN's policy I do not know. 

What we can anticipate is the boost I am included, which is about 2M in the package, but 20M after unzipped. 
I am inclined to put it there and try first.  If we do not include, if CRAN can build rstan, the user need to specify the boost.lib using parameter boost_lib during calling stan.  If CRAN cannot build rstan, then it will be a trouble for users to get started with rstan.
